findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T are honoured when present, but contractless mode ignores them. `CreateContractlessMembers` takes every public read-write member and never consults `[IgnoreMember]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreDataMember]` or `[DataMember(Name)]` on T. For example, a public property marked `[IgnoreMember]` on T is still serialized by the generated formatter, which also differs from what the dynamic contractless resolver does for the same type.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicEdgeCaseTests.IgnoreMemberOnFormattedTypeIsHonoured: T has `[IgnoreMember] public int IgnoredSecret { get; set; }` and a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` partial formatter. On head the generated formatter source contains `IgnoredSecret`.

findings.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration, not its containing types. A formatter nested in a non-partial class passes every check and reports no diagnostic. The generated `partial class` part then cannot merge with the user's declaration, so the consumer's build breaks with compiler errors (missing `partial` on the outer type, or an unimplemented `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`) instead of getting MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicEdgeCaseTests.NestedFormatterInNonPartialOuterIsDiagnosedOrCompiles: `public class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<MyType> { } }`. On head there is no generator diagnostic, yet the output compilation has errors.

findings.claim: The new filter excludes `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` classes from hand-written formatter discovery (`FormatterDescriptor`). As a result, T is no longer known as formattable to the TypeCollector or analyzer path that relies on that discovery. If T is a source type without attributes and is used as a member type of a `[MessagePackObject]`, it now gets MsgPack003 or is treated as unformattable, even though a formatter for it is being generated. The ObjectSerializationInfo created for the generated formatter only feeds the resolver, not member analysis.

receipt_plan.detail: Trace how TypeCollector/MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer learns custom formatters. If it relies on the GeneratorUtilities formatter provider or FormatterDescriptor, then `[MessagePackObject] class Holder { [Key(0)] public MyType V { get; set; } }` plus a generated formatter for MyType reports MsgPack003 on head but not on base.

findings.claim: `GetInstanceMembers` keeps only the most-derived symbol of each name, and `IsPublicReadWrite` then requires a public `SetMethod` on that symbol. A derived class that overrides only the getter of a base `public virtual int X { get; set; }` exposes an override symbol whose `SetMethod` is null. X is therefore silently dropped from the contractless contract, although it is publicly read-write on T.

receipt_plan.detail: Set `class B { public virtual int X { get; set; } } class D : B { public override int X { get => 1; } }` as the formatted type D and inspect the generated formatter: X is absent.
